contract_rows.exact_normalized_target: **Corollary D1 — L032 Theorem 1.2.** For every \(d\ge3\), \(n\ge5\) and \(k_1,\ldots,k_{d-1}\ge2\) with \(\sum_i k_i\le n-1\), there is a regular rank-\(d\) polytope with automorphism group of exact order \(2^n\) and type \(\{2^{k_1},\ldots,2^{k_{d-1}}\}\).
**Corollary D2 — L035 Theorem 1.2.** For \(n\ge10\), \(s,t\ge2\) and \(s+t\le n-1\), there is a regular rank-three polytope of order \(2^n\) and type \(\{2^s,2^t\}\).

**Corollary D3 — L035 Theorem 1.3, all three parts and eight presentations.** Let \(n\ge10\). Every marked rank-three string C-group of order \(2^n\) and type \(\{4,2^{n-s}\}\), for \(s\in\{3,4,5\}\), is exactly one of the following marked presentations. Put \(m=2^{n-s}\), \(r=bc\), \(d_0=(ab)^2\), and \(z=r^{m/2}\). All have common relations
\[
a^2=b^2=c^2=(ac)^2=(ab)^4=r^m=1.
\]
For \(s=3\), add \([d_0,c]=z^\epsilon\), with \(\epsilon=0,1\), giving \(G_1,G_2\). For \(s=4\), add \([d_0,r^2]=z^\epsilon\), with \(\epsilon=0,1\), giving \(G_3,G_4\). For \(s=5\), add
\[
[a,r^2]^2=z^\beta,\qquad [a,r^4]=z^\nu,
\]
with \((\beta,\nu)=(0,0),(1,0),(0,1),(1,1)\), giving \(G_5,G_6,G_7,G_8\), respectively. Conversely each bare presentation has the stated exact order, type and IP; the alternatives are distinct as marked string C-groups.
contract_rows.application_derivation: A5.1–A5.2, complete models and bounded seed

contract_rows.exact_normalized_target: **Corollary D4 — F013 Theorem 1.1.** Every finite nondegenerate two-group string C-group of rank \(d\ge2\) admits a marked epimorphism onto the canonical string C-group \(G(C_d)\) of order \(2^{2d-1}\).
**Corollary D5 — F013 Theorem 1.2.** Every finite nondegenerate regular rank-\(d\) polytope with two-group automorphism group, \(d\ge2\), covers \(C_d\).
contract_rows.application_derivation: A2.4 and retained cover correspondence

contract_rows.exact_normalized_target: **Corollary D6 — F016 Theorem 5.1(a–d).** For \(d\ge3\) and \(n_3,\ldots,n_d\ge5\), there is a finite regular rank-\(d\) polytope whose consecutive rank-three sections are exactly \(\{4,4\}_{(n_3)},\ldots,\{4,4\}_{(n_d)}\), where each square map has automorphism group of order \(2^{n_j}\). Its group has order \(2^{\sum_{j=3}^d n_j-3(d-3)}\). For \(d\ge4\) it is \((d-4,d-1)\)-flat and hence flat. It has FAP with respect to its co-\((d-4)\)-faces, co-\((d-3)\)-faces and facets, with the rank-three co-\((-1)\)-face interpreted as the whole-polytope cut.
contract_rows.application_derivation: A4.2 path and separator bindings

contract_rows.exact_normalized_target:
**Corollary D7 — F016 Theorem 5.3.** The automorphism group in D6 is precisely the quotient of the universal regular polytope group of generalized type \(\{\{4,4\}_{(n_3)},\ldots,\{4,4\}_{(n_d)}\}\) by
\[
[(r_ir_{i+1})^2,(r_{i+2}r_{i+3})^2]=1
\quad(0\le i\le d-4).
\]
contract_rows.application_derivation: A4.3 and bare universal presentation/order bound

contract_rows.exact_normalized_target:
**Corollary D8 — F016 Theorem 6.1(a–b).** Let \(d\ge4\), \(n_3,\ldots,n_{d-1}\ge5\), and \(m_{d-1}\ge5\). There is an alternating semiregular rank-\(d\) polytope with regular facet types
\[
(n_3,\ldots,n_{d-2},n_{d-1}),\qquad
(n_3,\ldots,n_{d-2},m_{d-1}).
\]
Its full automorphism group has order
\[
2^{\sum_{j=3}^{d-2}n_j+n_{d-1}+m_{d-1}-3(d-3)}
\]
if the last parameters differ, and twice this order if they agree. At \(d=4\), the shared list is empty and the common facet of the two facets is a square. The remaining co-\((d-4)\)-section is not separately prescribed.
contract_rows.application_derivation: A4.2 fork fiber-isomorphism and geometric assembly

contract_rows.exact_normalized_target: **Corollary D9 — F016 Theorem 7.1.** For a regular input polytope of rank \(d\ge3\) whose group is a finite or infinite two-group in the source's convention, its free regular extension has rank \(d+1\) and finitely generated infinite automorphism group with every finite-order element of two-power order.

contract_rows.exact_normalized_target: **Corollary D10 — F016 Theorem 7.2.** For an oriented chiral input polytope of rank \(d\ge3\) with directly regular facets and finite or infinite two-group automorphism group, its free oriented chiral extension has rank \(d+1\) and a finitely generated infinite two-group in the same convention.

contract_rows.exact_normalized_target: **Corollary D11 — F016 Theorem 7.3.** Let two regular rank-\(d\) polytopes, \(d\ge3\), have isomorphic facets and finite or infinite two-group automorphism groups. Their universal alternating semiregular extension has rank \(d+1\) and finitely generated infinite two-group automorphism group, with the additional branch swap precisely when the two facets of the extension are isomorphic.
